articles.title: Barrios y Hancko recuperan el 'mando' del Atlético
articles.standfirst: Simeone vuelve a contar con su futbolista más diferencial y con el jugador de campo más utilizado. Grimaldo y Baena trabajan en el gimnasio
articles.summary: Simeone vuelve a contar con su futbolista más diferencial y con el jugador de campo más utilizado. Grimaldo y Baena trabajan en el gimnasio
articles.body: Aunque el Atlético sigue aún pendiente de los compromisos del grueso de internacionales y, sobre todo, de que no vayan en aumento los efectos del virus FIFA, Simeone también ha empezado a recuperar a sus primeros efectivos en la vuelta al trabajo. Así, pese a contar únicamente con ocho futbolistas del primer equipo sobre el verde, las dos últimas incorporaciones suponen una gran noticia: Barrios y Hancko regresan listos para formar el once del domingo en Getafe. Tras no llegar a participar en ninguno de los dos partidos de España, el futbolista más diferencial del Atlético recupera el mando en el centro del campo rojiblanco. Si bien es cierto que la intensidad de los entrenamientos con la selección no fue la misma de la que tuvieron Koke y Cardoso durante la semana pasada, Barrios ya acelera para acompañar a ambos en la visita al Coliseum. De igual modo, Hancko, el jugador de campo más utilizado por El Cholo (1.293 minutos, sólo superado por los 1.440 de Oblak), también llega descansado tras no participar en el segundo partido disputado por Eslovaquia, con lo que también será un fijo frente a los de Bordalás. Un alivio para Simeone teniendo en cuenta los problemas físicos que golpean a la defensa. Así, aunque el esguince en el tobillo de Pubill es leve, su concurso en Getafe resulta más que improbable, siendo el Viking, a la semana siguiente, el primer objetivo que se marca el catalán. El Cuti Romero, por su parte, continúa con su trabajo de recuperación al margen, con lo que aún es una incógnita para el domingo. Sí estarán listos Baena y Grimaldo, de vuelta a la disciplina rojiblanca pero para ejercitarse en el gimnasio. El 10, para recuperar físicamente tras el alto volumen de minutos que ha tenido con España; el lateral para reponerse del proceso gripal que le obligó a dejar la concentración con la selección.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 11
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 25-of-33, 355 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 14 carries, 55 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Fresno State) Week 11 Outcome: Win (37-35)

Following a 410-yard performance against Fresno State, redshirt sophomore Brad Jackson has eclipsed 3,000 total yards of offense for the second year in a row, and his 3,080 mark this season ranks 10th among all FBS quarterbacks.

After making the somewhat surprising decision to stay at Texas State last offseason on the heels of a 3,968-yard, 38-touchdown season in his first year as a starter, it will be interesting to see if he enters the transfer portal this time around.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 19-of-35, 174 yards, 1 TD, 3 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 35 yards, 1 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (LSU) Week 11 Outcome: Win (22-21)

Arch Manning led a 12-play, 58-yard drive capped off by a four-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown with three seconds remaining to give Texas a comeback victory and keep the Longhorns alive in the College Football Playoff picture.

The dramatic finish came in a game where Manning threw a season-high three picks, and he now has 19 touchdowns and 10 interceptions on the year. It has not been the Heisman-caliber campaign many were expecting, but Texas is still 8-2 overall.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 32-of-58, 340 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 0 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Tulsa) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (21-38)

Caden Veltkamp ranks among the FBS leaders in completions (276, 1st), passing yards (3,086, 4th) and passing touchdowns (29, 2nd), and after throwing 17 interceptions a year ago, he has been picked off just six times this year.

He eclipsed 10,000 career passing yards in Saturday's game, as he is in his third year as a starter after one season at Western Kentucky and now two years piloting the Owls' offense.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 27-of-37, 244 yards, 2 TD, 3 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, -3 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Texas) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (21-22)

For the second time this season, Sam Leavitt threw three interceptions in a game, and this time around the end result was a loss that almost certainly eliminated LSU from the College Football Playoff picture.

The prized transfer portal pickup leads the SEC with 3,134 total yards and 27 total touchdowns, but he is also tied for the FBS lead with 12 interceptions. He threw just nine picks total over 20 games in his two seasons at Arizona State.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 17-of-34, 270 yards, 2 TD, 2 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, -8 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Stanford) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (22-40)

With 2,701 passing yards, Ethan Grunkemeyer is on track to become just the fourth 3,000-yard passer in Virginia Tech history, and the first since Jerod Evans set the record with 3,546 yards in 2016.

Unfortunately, he had his second multi-interception game of the season on Saturday, and the Hokies have now lost back-to-back games and four of their last six overall.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 18-of-24, 252 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 6 yards, 1 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Missouri) Week 11 Outcome: Win (48-21)

After throwing two interceptions in a loss to Auburn and throwing for a season-low 101 yards against Florida the following week, Gunner Stockton has completed 69.2 percent of his passes for 438 yards with five passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and zero interceptions against Ole Miss and Missouri.

He leads the SEC in completion percentage (71.4), passing touchdowns (21), yards per attempt (9.6) and passer rating (179.8).

Week 11 Passing Stats: 23-of-31, 154 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 14 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (North Carolina) Week 11 Outcome: Win (16-14)

Over the last three weeks, Lincoln Kienholz has completed 71.4 percent of his passes for 586 yards with five touchdowns and zero interceptions, adding another 157 yards and a score on the ground.

That strong stretch of individual play has been part of a five-game winning streak for Louisville, including three road wins, following a disappointing 2-3 start to the year.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 19-of-34, 227 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 25 carries, 36 yards, 1 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Kansas) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (14-37)

Michael Hawkins Jr. ranks 16th in the nation and second among quarterbacks with 960 rushing yards this season, and his 20 rushing touchdowns lead all players, one more than Duke star running back Nate Sheppard. He was shut down on Saturday, though, averaging just 1.4 yards per carry.

On top of his ground production this year, he has also tallied 2,128 yards and 13 touchdowns through the air. Unfortunately, that offensive firepower has been largely undermined by a defense that is allowing 34.8 points per game.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 13-of-25, 204 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 14 carries, 100 yards, 2 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Arizona) Week 11 Outcome: Win (40-39)

A 70-yard touchdown strike from Devon Dampier to Creed Whittemore with 2:35 remaining proved to be the game-winning score in a Big 12 shootout with Arizona, and for the fourth time this season Dampier contributed four total touchdowns.

With 2,257 passing yards, 582 rushing yards and 31 total touchdowns, Dampier has led Utah to a 10-0 start and the top spot in the Big 12 conference race. He could emerge as a bona fide Heisman candidate with more of the same in the coming weeks.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 26-of-42, 311 yards, 1 TD, 3 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 0 carries, 0 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Indiana) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (13-27)

Jayden Maiava threw three interceptions for the first time in his two seasons at USC, and the Trojans suffered their second loss in the last three weeks following a 6-1 start that saw them climb as high as No. 12 in the AP poll.

A good Indiana secondary that is allowing less than 200 passing yards per game deserves credit, and despite the dud, Maiava still leads the Big Ten in passing yards (2,835) and passing touchdowns (21).

Week 11 Passing Stats: 20-of-28, 217 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -7 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Boston College) Week 11 Outcome: Win (41-7)

CJ Carr threw for 2,741 yards and 24 touchdowns last season in 12 games, and he has almost surpassed both marks through 10 games this season with 2,385 yards and 23 touchdowns during the Fighting Irish's 9-1 start.

He has at least 200 passing yards and two touchdowns in seven of 10 games so far this season, and he will go head-to-head with another high-profile quarterback in Kevin Jennings next weekend when Notre Dame hosts SMU.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 15-of-31, 313 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 73 yards, 2 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (South Florida) Week 11 Outcome: Win (52-41)

Since a Week 7 loss to Tulane when he threw three interceptions, Marcus Stokes has racked up 1,004 passing yards with 10 touchdowns and zero interceptions in wins over East Carolina, Army and South Florida.

He leads the AAC and ranks second in the nation with 33 total touchdowns, and he has been one of the most productive transfer quarterbacks in the country while making the leap from the D-II West Florida.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 10-of-20, 125 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 10 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (UTSA) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (16-35)

Tayven Jackson left Saturday's game against UTSA with an injury during the first drive of the second half, and he returned to the sidelines later with his arm in a sling.

The injury is feared to be season-ending, according to Matt Zenitz of CBSSports. If that's the case, his 2026 campaign will end with 3,005 passing yards and 23 touchdowns after he transferred from UCF in the offseason.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 22-of-33, 217 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 1 yard Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Vanderbilt) Week 11 Outcome: Win (21-6)

For his third straight game and fifth time in eight SEC conference games, Keelon Russell threw three passing touchdowns, and his 21 total are tied for the SEC lead with Austin Simmons (Missouri) and Gunner Stockton (Georgia).

A matchup with FCS opponent Chattanooga next weekend should give him an opportunity to pad his stats, and he remains on the periphery of the Heisman Trophy conversation for the 8-2 Crimson Tide.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 14-of-25, 201 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 34 yards, 2 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (SMU) Week 11 Outcome: Win (49-7)

The Demon Deacons rank second in the nation with 43.9 points per game during their 9-1 start to the year, and they padded that mark on Saturday with a surprising blowout of a ranked SMU team.

A rushing attack that averages 186.8 yards per game has helped open up the passing game for Gio Lopez, who has 2,377 yards and 19 touchdowns against just one interception. That said, he has also played a major role in the running game, ranking third on the team with 351 rushing yards to go along with eight scores.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 27-of-43, 356 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, -16 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Utah) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (39-40)

Noah Fifita eclipsed 3,000 yards passing for the second straight season with another 300-yard passing game on Saturday, though it wasn't enough to pull off the upset against undefeated Utah.

He led a 91-yard touchdown drive to give Arizona the lead with 3:13 remaining in the fourth quarter, but the defense gave up the go-ahead score two plays later, and the ensuing Wildcats drive stalled with a four-play turnover on downs.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 26-of-42, 272 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 29 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Colorado) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (32-42)

Conner Weigman has already matched last season's 25 passing touchdowns in three fewer games, and he has done it with a nice uptick in his yards per attempt (7.6 to 8.5) and passer rating (147.1 to 162.8).

His 32 total touchdowns trail only Drew Mestemaker (36), Michael Hawkins Jr. (33) and Marcus Stokes (33), though an interception and a lost fumble on Saturday contributed to Colorado's upset victory.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 22-of-35, 209 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, -5 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Wake Forest) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (7-49)

With five punts, two turnovers on downs, two lost fumbles and an interception, the SMU offense never found any semblance of momentum on Saturday, and it was already 42-0 when they finally put points on the board.

It was only the second time this season that Kevin Jennings failed to contribute multiple touchdowns, and the Mustangs lost both of those games. A third loss effectively knocks them out of the ACC race, but they can still play spoiler this weekend by handing Notre Dame its second loss of the year.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 30-of-41, 382 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 7 yards Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Duke) Week 11 Outcome: Win (36-25)

Darian Mensah led the ACC in passing yards (3,973) and passing touchdowns (34) last season while piloting the Duke offense, and on Saturday he racked up 382 passing yards against his former team to help Miami improve to 9-1 on the year.

With star wide receiver Malachi Toney sidelined, former Duke teammate Cooper Bartake has become Mensah's go-to target in the passing game. After logging nine catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns against Notre Dame, he had eight receptions for 134 yards on Saturday.

Week 11 Passing Stats: 27-of-42, 277 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT Week 11 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, -8 yards, 1 TD Week 11 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Texas Tech) Week 11 Outcome: Loss (27-52)

With multiple interceptions for the first time since Week 2 and fewer than 300 passing yards for just the second time all year, Saturday's loss to a very good Texas Tech team is unlikely to be a focal point of any future Drew Mestemaker highlight reel.

Zooming out, he still leads the nation in passing yards (3,239) and passing touchdowns (30), though his 10 interceptions are now also tops in the Big 12. He has put himself in the conversation to be the first quarterback taken in the 2027 NFL draft, despite a 6-4 showing from the Cowboys.

articles.title: 'Have you figured it out?': Ronaldo challenges fans to decode meaning behind his cryptic 'M' finger gesture
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's mysterious 'M' finger gesture sparks fan speculation about its meaning as he nears the milestone of 1,000 career goals in Saudi Pro League.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has made a habit of turning goals into celebrations, but his latest gesture has left supporters trying to work out what he is signalling. The Al-Nassr forward has now asked fans directly if they have figured it out, adding to speculation that the repeated hand sign could have something to do with the milestone he is chasing.Ronaldo asks fans to decipher his mysterious hand gestureRonaldo reignited the discussion after sharing a video on Instagram in which he appears in a white polo shirt, smiling at the camera while making an unusual sign with his fingers."Have you figured it out yet?" he wrote, adding eyes and laughing emojis.It is not the first time the 41-year-old has used the gesture. He was spotted making the same sign after Al-Nassr's victory over Neom on October 21, prompting the Saudi club to share a video asking supporters to guess its meaning. He then repeated it during his hat-trick in the 5-3 win over Al-Kholood on October 29.The gesture appears to form the letter 'M', and one theory has attracted particular attention: it could represent 1,000 in Roman numerals. The Portuguese word for thousand, mil, also begins with the same letter, adding another possible link to the milestone.Sports social media account 433 has also highlighted the Roman numeral theory, which has gained traction as Ronaldo approaches four figures in career goals. Al-Nassr chief executive Jose Semedo has been seen making the same gesture alongside the forward, further fuelling speculation that it carries a message.Another suggestion is that it could be connected to Ronaldo's son Mateo. However, neither Ronaldo nor Al-Nassr has confirmed what the gesture means, leaving all explanations speculative for now.Ronaldo is 15 goals away from reaching 1,000The timing has made the milestone theory difficult for supporters to ignore. Ronaldo currently has 985 official senior career goals for club and country, leaving him 15 short of becoming the first player to reach 1,000 goals in official senior football.He reached that total after scoring his 983rd, 984th and 985th goals in Al-Nassr's victory over Al-Kholood on October 29. The hat-trick took his tally to 985 in 1,343 senior appearances, underlining the scale of a career that has stretched across more than two decades.Having recently brought his international career to a close, Ronaldo can now concentrate on his club commitments with Al-Nassr as he continues his pursuit of the landmark.Al-Nassr face Al-Ahli next in Saudi Pro LeagueRonaldo's next opportunity to add to his tally comes against Al-Ahli Saudi on Friday, November 20, in the Saudi Pro League. The match is scheduled for 11pm IST.Al-Nassr go into the fixture second in the league standings, two points behind leaders Al-Hilal. The meeting with Al-Ahli offers another important test as the club look to maintain their challenge at the top of the table.For Ronaldo, the immediate focus will be on extending his goal tally, while the mystery surrounding his latest gesture continues to provide fans with another talking point. articles.title: Vinicius: "Estaba acordado que jugaría 15 minutos más, siempre quiero marcar más goles"
articles.standfirst: El madridista se marchó contrariado después de ser sustituido en el 60 ante Singapur
articles.summary: El madridista se marchó contrariado después de ser sustituido en el 60 ante Singapur
articles.body: Vinicius Junior está de vuelta. El atacante del Real Madrid, que venía de lograr un doblete en la derrota contra Japón (3-2), se reivindicó firmando su primer 'hat-trick' con Brasil en el 0-7 sobre Singapur. "Es mi primer 'hat-trick', el primero de muchos espero. Entramos muy concentrados, parecía fácil pero luego hay que jugar bien y crear ocasiones. Estoy contento con los goles y con la victoria. Ahora toca volver a centrarme en mi club y estar al 100%", aseguró Vini, que podrá reaparecer en LaLiga contra el Celta después de cumplir la sanción de cuatro partidos que le fue impuesta por el tirón de pelo a Nathan-Dylan Saliba en el partido contra el Villarreal. El madridista cierra 2026 con 11 goles con la 'Seleçao'. Nadie, desde Neymar en 2014, había marcado tanto goles con Brasil en un año natural. Es, también, el máximo goleador de la 'era Ancelotti': acumula 13 goles en 20 partidos. Cabe recordar que, en total, acumula 19 dianas en 59 internacionalidades. Los seis restantes los anotó con Dorival Jr. (3), Tite (2) y Ramón Menezes (1). Sin embargo, Vinicius, con Carlo Ancelotti, sancionado, en la grada, se marchó contrariado después de abandonar el campo en el minuto 60: "Estaba acordado que jugaría 15 minutos más, pero siempre quiero marcar más goles". En cualquier caso, se mostraba satisfecho con el desempeño Brasil en su último amistoso del año y optimista de cara al futuro: "Estoy contento porque todo el mundo ha participado. Jugaron todos y ahora toca pensar en la Copa América".

articles.title: Fan Convicted of Racially Insulting Mbappé at Spanish League Game
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — A fan has been convicted of racially insulting Kylian Mbappé during a Spanish league game last year, Real Madrid said Tuesday.
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — A fan has been convicted of racially insulting Kylian Mbappé during a Spanish league game last year, Real Madrid said Tuesday.

Madrid said the fan was convicted of a hate crime and given a suspended prison sentence of 11 months following the insults directed at Mbappé in a match against Oviedo at Carlos Tartiere stadium in August 2025.

The fan, who was not named in the club's statement, was also fined. The sentence was suspended on condition the fan stay away from soccer stadiums for two years.

Other fans have previously been convicted for racial insults against Madrid players, including forward Vinícius Júnior.

articles.title: Arsenal news: Piero Hincapie set for new contract
articles.summary: Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.
articles.body:
Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.

Hincapie, 24, joined the Gunners last summer from Bayer Leverkusen, initially on loan, with the Gunners activating an option to make the move permanent at the end of the season.

The Ecuador international has established himself as a key member of Mikel Arteta's squad, making 47 appearances in all competitions.

The versatile defender's existing deal still has over four years left to run - but he is now set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms.

Elsewhere, the club intend to open talks with left-back Riccardo Calafiori, 24, over renewing his deal.

The Italy international has become a crucial part of Arteta's plans since his arrival from Bologna in 2024.

His current deal expires in the summer of 2029, but it is expected talks over an extension will begin in the not too distant future.

Arsenal are on a contract renewal drive, with the club set to confirm new deals for Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice and goalkeeper David Raya.

articles.title: Infantino’s FIFA challenger Diallo claims to have support beyond Europe
articles.summary: French football chief Philippe Diallo says he has received ‘spontaneous signs of strong support’ against Infantino.
articles.body:
French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo says he has the backing of countries beyond Europe in his bid to depose Gianni Infantino in the upcoming FIFA presidential election.

“To beat him you need 106 votes, which is a majority,” Diallo said on Tuesday following his nomination as the European governing body UEFA’s representative.

“It is now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents, but already since yesterday I have received spontaneous signs of strong support which will be revealed in the coming days.”

Diallo was speaking in Paris the day after accepting an invitation from UEFA to stand against Infantino in the election to be held next March.

UEFA, which has 55 member associations, said that European nations had “unanimously pledged their full support” to Diallo, ahead of Wednesday’s deadline for candidates to declare themselves.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors was revealed in July.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but UEFA has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of “criminal mismanagement” against the current FIFA president in Switzerland.

Diallo announced in September that the French Football Federation (FFF) was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election, following similar announcements from other European associations. At the time he said that “the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed”.

“There can no longer be a type of single-handed governance where the biggest issues in football are decided behind the scenes, without any transparency and without anyone being consulted, without going through the executive committee,” Diallo, 63, said on Tuesday.

“My vision will be one of open, collegiate governance, in which the different bodies really play their part.”

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Arsene Wenger, the French former Arsenal manager and FIFA’s current chief of global football development, had at one point been seen as a potential candidate who could get Europe’s backing, but he will not stand.

FIFA has a total of 211 member associations, with each having one vote in the presidential election. A majority is needed for a candidate to win.

articles.title: Romario demands Ancelotti sacking as war of words continues
articles.summary: Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo publicly demands that legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties.
articles.body:
Few would have predicted that Carlo Ancelotti would be facing the wrath of a Brazil legend just 18 months into his tenure as head coach of the Brazil national team.

But Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo, has publicly demanded that legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties not once but twice in the last week alone.

It all started after Brazil suffered a 3-2 friendly defeat by Japan on Friday thanks to a controversial stoppage-time winner from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.

Ancelotti received a red card for dissent in the aftermath - the first of his international management career, as Barcelona forward Raphinha also saw red.

And in the wake of that defeat, despite it being a friendly, Romario quickly took to social media to air his frustrations about the former Real Madrid boss.

"Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and leave!" he wrote on Instagram.

"Nobody questions your history. You are one of the greatest coaches world football has ever seen, but that was at club level."

Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, a result which ensured they failed to qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time since 1990.

And Romario alluded to this too, stating that the country "can't take the risk of throwing another World Cup in the trash - the time to act is now!"

The Brazil boss has been in the game long enough to know how to deal with all sorts of opinions.

He has won the Champions League a record five times as a head coach and won the league title in all of Europe's top five divisions, along with multiple domestic cups.

But his record with Brazil is far from perfect. Across 21 matches, they have recorded 12 wins, four draws and five defeats.

However, while Ancelotti acknowledges the need for improvement, he emphasised the fact that it is still "a new project."

Speaking before Brazil's friendly with Singapore on Tuesday the Italian said: "In a democratic country with freedom of speech, everyone is allowed to express their opinion.

"It's not up to me to say whether the things he says are correct, wrong or just stupid. The truth is that Romario talks a lot. A lot. It's his right."

Despite the criticism he has faced, Ancelotti feels Brazil are on the right track and who is to tell him otherwise when you look at his track record?

"I really like what we're doing," he said.

You would have thought that would have been enough to let it lie for the time being.

But before Brazil had even kicked a ball in their next friendly against Singapore, Romario was speaking out again.

The former striker, who is the ninth-highest goalscorer in football history with 784 goals, doubled down on his calls for Ancelotti to be sacked.

"I talk a lot because when it comes to the national team, I have size, weight and power of speech," Romario, 60, said.

"I do not speak to gain followers, I do not speak for people to like me. I speak my mind.

"I have worn this shirt for many years and I am pretty sure I was one of the ones that helped the little yellow be respected all over the world."

He said he respected Ancelotti but added he hadn't "added anything new" to the national side.

"We will find another coach who will do a better job than you. And I'm saying this to your face, not through a message, including to the president of the CBF, who is long overdue to fire you."

Brazil faced Singapore in their final match of 2026 on Tuesday and won 7-0 .

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior, who has come under scrutiny of his own so far this season, scored a hat-trick within the opening 21 minutes while Bournemouth winger Rayan and Chelsea's Estevao were also on the scoresheet.

It's a result that may bring a pause to proceedings in this war of words for now. However, if this last seven days has proved anything, it's that this saga is likely far from over.

articles.title: Vinicius Jr. explains substitution frustration after Brazil hat-trick vs Singapore: ‘I always want to play more’
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior returned to the spotlight with Brazil after scoring a hat-trick in the 7-0 victory over Singapore, but the Real Madrid forward also attracted...
articles.body:
Vinicius Junior returned to the spotlight with Brazil after scoring a hat-trick in the 7-0 victory over Singapore, but the Real Madrid forward also attracted attention for his visible frustration when he was substituted around the hour mark.

The 26-year-old had scored three times in the opening 21 minutes, completing his first hat-trick for the national team.

However, his evening ended earlier than he expected, prompting questions about his reaction.

Vinicius wanted more minutes after completing Brazil hat-trick

Vinicius subsequently explained that he had hoped to remain on the pitch longer, although he admitted that he understood the decision made by Carlo Ancelotti.

"It was agreed that I would play 15 or 20 more minutes. I always want to play more, score more goals," said Vinicius, as per Mundo Deportivo .

Vinicius has explained his frustration regarding his Brazil substitution. (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images)

He added that he was "Happy because everyone participated. I understood that more people needed to play."

The forward was equally pleased with the milestone, describing it as his first hat-trick for Brazil and hoping it would be the first of many.

"My first hat-trick, hopefully of many. We went in very focused. It seemed easy, but you have to create chances. I could have scored more, but I'm happy with the goals and the win.

"Now it's time to focus on my club and think about the Copa America," he added.

Real Madrid forward rediscovers scoring touch with Brazil

The performance completed an encouraging international break for Vinicius, who scored five goals across two friendlies.

Vinicius scored five goals in two matches for Brazil. (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images)

He had previously netted twice against Japan in Brazil's 3-2 defeat before producing three goals against Singapore. Notably, he also had another effort ruled out during the Singapore match.

For what it is worth, it was a welcome return to scoring form for Vinicius after a difficult spell at club level, having netted a solitary goal under Mourinho this season.

Mourinho faces Vinicius decision ahead of Celta fixture

Vinicius now returns to Real Madrid after completing his four-match La Liga suspension.

He is eligible again for Saturday's home meeting with Celta Vigo on November 21, giving Mourinho the option of restoring him to the starting XI.

Notably, the decision will not be an easy one for the Portuguese manager because Yan Diomande has performed admirably during the Brazilian's absence and changing the rhythm will bring obvious caveats for the team.
